metadata.name: Ecodesign for C++
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for C++ code: copies avoided, suitable containers, RAII, buffered I/O, no busy waiting.

copies.name: C++ — copies and allocations
copies.description: Copy only what must be copied (RGESN Algorithms, GR491_Backend_4).

rules.title: Non-trivial object passed by value
rules.description: Passing a string or a vector by value copies the entire content on every call.
rules.recommendation: Pass by const&; std::move to transfer ownership; non-owning views (std::string_view, std::span) to read without copying.

rules.title: vector without reserve() or emplace
rules.description: A vector that grows through reallocation copies its whole content at every doubling; push_back of a temporary adds one more copy.
rules.recommendation: reserve() when the size is predictable, emplace_back rather than push_back of a temporary; reuse buffers (clear() keeps the capacity).

rules.title: shared_ptr by default
rules.description: The atomic reference counter of shared_ptr costs on every copy, usually for ownership that is in fact unique.
rules.recommendation: unique_ptr by default, shared_ptr only when ownership is genuinely shared; RAII throughout.

conteneurs.name: C++ — containers and algorithms
conteneurs.description: Choose the structure that fits the actual access pattern (RGESN 9.1).

rules.title: Repeated linear search
rules.description: std::find on a large vector is linear; repeated, the processing turns quadratic.
rules.recommendation: unordered_map/unordered_set for frequent lookups; STL and ranges algorithms rather than successive copies.

rules.title: File loaded entirely into memory
rules.description: Reading a whole file into a string consumes memory proportional to its size, where a stream would process it in blocks.
rules.recommendation: Buffered, block-based I/O, and streaming for large volumes.

rules.title: Busy waiting
rules.description: A polling loop keeps a CPU core busy and prevents low-power states.
rules.recommendation: condition_variable, poll/epoll or async primitives; build production with optimisations and profile before any manual optimisation.
